# Milestone native session — 2026-09-09

The recorded `06dad49` release process completed an 18-minute resource observation with 12 minutes of operator-paced mixed review. RSS increased as more views were exercised, from 184.609 MiB to 269.703 MiB, with a 269.766 MiB maximum. The final 40 seconds of Projects idle remained within a 0.047 MiB band. This is a short final plateau, not evidence of a constant-memory warm loop or a long-term leak-free process.

## Executable and source identity

- Source: `06dad49fc61fee3b0bd786f2b4a8cf8661817b30`; the build manifest recorded a clean source status and identical before/after maps of all 399 collected inputs, including both vendored Rust dependencies.
- Compiled-input map SHA-256: `02720fb4c5081052d5856ef90e3d35053b98c9b5f5bd6ae490292440779e9dc2`.
- Raw release executable SHA-256: `788f3e47548b8b27ae75ea932e5a530fd701a399a8a35872e2ad61c818188f5f`.
- Exercised package executable SHA-256: `345d941e011d1fd0cfee71942be3b88a47deee0665978f77da4323bb21ba26ec`. Both manifest entries have Mach-O UUID `7BA32F76-D1AD-3A16-AD33-3B4F47C03F6B` (arm64). The sampler verified this packaged executable unchanged at the end.
- Exercised bundle: `/tmp/gitturtle-consistency-20260909/ConsistencyQA.app`; PID `88597`, process start reported by macOS `ps` as `Wed Sep 9 10:23:47 2026` (MDT). The app was already running for approximately 4 minutes 41 seconds when sampling started. This is not a cold launch measurement.
- Hardware: Apple M4 Max, Mac16,5, 16 logical CPUs, 128 GiB RAM, arm64. macOS 26.6.2 (25G83).

The package and raw executable hashes are recorded separately; the resource samples match the package hash. This report uses the existing release build and operator evidence. Analysis did not launch the app, rebuild it, manipulate its UI, or modify its repositories.

The stop-file footer is `2026-09-09T16:46:35.010162+00:00` at elapsed 1086.620 seconds. No collection errors or process-identity changes were recorded. The planned 20-minute maximum was not reached; the observer stopped normally after about 18 minutes 7 seconds.

The active action span is 16:33:47.386–16:45:52.512, approximately 12 minutes 5 seconds, with ordinary operator pauses. The written protocol lists planned activities; it is not proof that each happened. In particular, this interval’s action record does not establish a PDF preview activation. Broader native QA belongs to the coordinator’s validation record.

The log snapshot contains 699 UI-tool records, of which 631 began inside the resource interval: 599 target GitTurtle and 32 target System Settings. These comprise 392 state captures and 239 actions (143 clicks, 51 key presses, 31 text entries, 9 scrolls, 4 drags and 1 paste). One paste at 16:35:27 failed with a tooling timeout waiting for clipboard consumption; the operator subsequently typed the path and opened the repository. Its failure is retained. A successful UI-tool return is not a product assertion or a latency sample.

The main large fixture was `/tmp/gitturtle-consistency-20260909/large`; a passive post-session check found HEAD `bcf41e2d24ff5582a145be5d34ebbdca774c95b4`, tree `1a0d82c51d27d43d6d6428ffef9658a2466e51fc`, 653 commits reachable from all refs and 94 refs. The expanded fixture was `/private/tmp/gitturtle-expanded-native-20260909`, HEAD `6d2a5f953fee3b43ee45a76323fd67df9ae20e31`, tree `08f8a78d3e617f874c2b74851aa57623a5ad19cc` (two commits). Those checks identify the retained fixtures; they do not reconstruct every mutable working byte at each action. The recovery and local HTTP fixtures were task-owned. No equal baseline workload or cache reset was run for this session.

During the short repeated Quick Open sequence, sampled RSS rose from 250.906 MiB at 16:44:23.467 to 263.469 MiB at 16:44:28.514 and 269.234 MiB at 16:44:33.463. Therefore the repeated warm sequence did not demonstrate a flat allocation footprint. The observer cannot attribute this growth to decoders, editor allocations, allocator retention, cached content, GPU-related host storage, or a leak.

The final Projects-idle samples ranged from 269.703 to 269.750 MiB. Its first CPU interval includes the transition to Projects (2.800%); the following eight intervals had a 0% median and 0.2002% maximum. Threads settled to 12, fresh FD observations stayed at 9, and one Git child remained. This supports a short settled endpoint after mixed coverage. It does not establish eventual cache release, a process-wide memory cap, behavior over hours, or stable memory under many repeated preview cycles.

## Observation overhead and background load

The read-only sampler used `ps` every 5 seconds, `ps -M` for thread counts and `lsof` every 30 seconds. Command collection took a median 88.448 ms, p95 138.214 ms and maximum 364.817 ms (16:41:33.758). Schedule lag was at most 9.138 ms. These are observer costs, not application work durations.

No compiler process was detected in any of the 218 system snapshots. The coordinator had completed macOS builds and stopped task containers before sampling. Docker-named background processes remained present in every snapshot (9, once 10); names alone do not establish running containers. Desktop work continued: one-minute load ranged from 5.352 to 19.417. Sampled background peaks included Codex Renderer 185.3%, Slack Renderer 131.8%, Chrome Renderer 117.0%, WindowServer 68.3%, and System Settings 53.0%. Those `ps` values can exceed 100% across cores and are point observations rather than continuous competing-load measurements.

The observations are not atomic. Short-lived children, brief FD/thread spikes and sub-5-second CPU bursts can fall between samples. RSS excludes GPU/driver allocations and cannot attribute retained memory to an app cache. No native frame-rate, completed GPU work or input-to-display timing was measured by the resource sampler.

## Frame traces: separate whole-process evidence

The app trace records elapsed time from the relevant selection/activation handler through the next GPUI frame callback after prepared content and synchronous editor setup. The [implementation](../../crates/app/src/main.rs) checks generation and mode before emitting. Commit-file-list and file-preview metrics are separate; Working Changes preview starts at file activation and excludes the preceding status refresh or Git write. Input delivery before the handler, OS presentation and GPU completion are outside the boundary. Superseded or missing callbacks are not zero-duration samples.

The trace has no timestamps, event IDs, repository identities or cache labels. The frozen file contains 25 ordered samples from this release process as captured at 16:49:41 UTC, including follow-on interaction after resource sampling stopped. It cannot be split reliably into resource phases, paired one-to-one with UI records, or described as 25 timed-session actions. All values are retained below as separate whole-process evidence.

| Trace metric | Count | Median ms | p95 ms | Maximum ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `commit_files_frame_ms` | 14 | 42.498 | 64.282 | 64.282 |
| `file_preview_frame_ms` | 6 | 42.665 | 228.714 | 228.714 |
| `working_preview_frame_ms` | 5 | 74.897 | 111.086 | 111.086 |

The 228.714 ms file-preview maximum remains included. With fewer than 20 samples in each metric, nearest-rank p95 equals the observed maximum. The log cannot identify which file, cold/warm state or concurrent activity caused that maximum. These heterogeneous sparse samples support no before/after speedup claim. The earlier `baseline-summary.json` remains exploratory and noncomparable: different actions, uncontrolled cache/load conditions and no valid event pairing.
